claim_summary: Conditional on the saved uniform two-way O_(M,B)(N^-1/2) channel theorem between the critical spin family and the quartic R^3 observation, R independent N-spin blocks have Le Cam distance at most O_(M,B)(R N^-1/2) from R classical observations.
For every [0,1]-bounded loss, optimal Bayes and minimax risks differ by at most the channel error; hence no nonvanishing bounded-loss quantum decision advantage remains for R=o(sqrt(N)).

The quartic observation is a regular exponential family in b with Fisher matrix Cov(X), uniformly finite and positive definite; at A=b=0 the diagonal information is (sqrt(3)/6) Gamma(5/4)/Gamma(3/4) = 0.213523984564... .
status_reason: The decision and Fisher derivations are internal; the uniform two-way O(N^-1/2) channel bound is inherited from the source-derived N20 package and has not received external validation or priority review.

executable_evidence.scope: Numerically evaluates only the exact gamma expression for the classical Fisher-information constant at A=b=0.
